steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

title: Keeping Inference in the Radio: Design and Measurement of a Spiking Accelerator for mmWave ISAC Activity Recognition
summary: Replaces general-purpose-processor inference on base stations or handsets with a fully on-FPGA spiking classifier, allowing the main processors to sleep during always-on activity sensing. Costs include RFSoC programmable-logic hardware (ZCU208), a spike-encoding front end, and 3-bit quantized weights within half a point of the 6-bit baseline. It can fail because results are specific to a small 132-neuron model on one public 60 GHz dataset, require FPGA toolchain expertise and hardware the reader likely does not operate, and do not transfer to GPU- or API-based ML production workloads.
rationale: The technique targets FPGA-based RF sensing hardware, not GPU or API inference, so it falls outside the reader's production scope despite its strong energy claims.
technique: Spiking neural network accelerator for always-on mmWave sensing

claims.statement: Replaces general-purpose-processor inference on base stations or handsets with a fully on-FPGA spiking classifier, allowing the main processors to sleep during always-on activity sensing. Costs include RFSoC programmable-logic hardware (ZCU208), a spike-encoding front end, and 3-bit quantized weights within half a point of the 6-bit baseline. It can fail because results are specific to a small 132-neuron model on one public 60 GHz dataset, require FPGA toolchain expertise and hardware the reader likely does not operate, and do not transfer to GPU- or API-based ML production workloads.

The SNN requires an eighth of the logic and 3.4x less dynamic energy per decision than a same-topology conventional network fed identical binary spikes, and 7.6x less than one fed 16-bit spectrograms, at comparable accuracy (94.7% accuracy, 206 us inference).
